tiers.name: Icon of the Decade
tiers.overview:
The NESA-Africa Icon of the Decade tier recognises individuals or eligible institutions whose exceptional, sustained and transformative contributions have significantly advanced education in Africa.

This tier celebrates educational legacy rather than isolated achievements. It acknowledges contributions that have influenced educational access, philanthropy, literacy, curriculum development, technical education or the long-term development of learners and institutions.

Recognition should reflect a substantial body of work whose significance can be demonstrated through credible evidence and whose benefits extend beyond a single campaign, project or public appearance.
tiers.why:
Africa's educational progress has been shaped by people and institutions that invest resources, develop knowledge, strengthen educational systems and create opportunities for future generations.

Recognising these contributions helps preserve educational history, inspire responsible philanthropy, encourage long-term investment and highlight approaches that others may learn from.

It also reinforces the principle that educational leadership should be assessed through lasting contribution rather than wealth, popularity or status alone.
evidence: Sustained commitment: A substantial record of contribution over time.
Transformative educational value: Significant improvements in educational opportunity, practice, institutions or knowledge.
Documented outcomes: Credible evidence of beneficiaries, resources, programmes or measurable educational changes.
Leadership and influence: Evidence that the nominee's work inspired, enabled or strengthened wider educational efforts.
Enduring legacy: Benefits that remain relevant beyond the original intervention.
Integrity and credibility: Verifiable claims, responsible stewardship and appropriate independent evidence.

tiers.name: Influencer Awards
tiers.overview:
The NESA-Africa Influencer Awards recognise prominent personalities who have used their public influence, creative talent, professional achievements or audience reach to make meaningful contributions to education.

This tier focuses on the conversion of influence into educational benefit.

It recognises individuals whose activities help learners access opportunities, mobilise educational support, promote literacy, encourage school participation, finance educational programmes or increase public awareness of important education challenges.

The emphasis is not on celebrity status but on what the nominee has achieved for education through that influence.
tiers.why:
Sports personalities, musicians and digital influencers can communicate with audiences that traditional educational institutions may struggle to reach.

Their platforms can inspire young people, mobilise funding, attract volunteers, promote positive educational behaviour and amplify the needs of underserved learners.

When public influence is responsibly directed towards education, it can become a valuable tool for social development.
evidence: Clear educational purpose: Activities directly connected to education or learning.
Effective use of influence: Evidence that the nominee mobilised attention, resources, participation or support.
Real educational beneficiaries: Identifiable learners, institutions or communities that benefited.
Verified achievements: Scholarships, campaigns, educational content, mentoring or other documented contributions.
Credible engagement: Meaningful educational action rather than follower counts or promotional impressions alone.
Continuity or significance: Sustained engagement or an intervention with substantial verified results.

tiers.name: Platinum Awards
tiers.overview:
The NESA-Africa Platinum Awards recognise outstanding institutions, public leaders, partnerships, research initiatives and education programmes whose work contributes meaningfully to educational quality, access, knowledge development or system improvement.

This tier emphasises the capacity to design, manage and deliver effective educational interventions.

It recognises contributions in tertiary education libraries, research and development, faith-based education, political leadership, international partnerships and diaspora engagement.

Platinum recognition should reflect credible institutional or programme performance, not merely organisational size or reputation.
tiers.why:
Education systems require more than financial investment. They depend on capable institutions, reliable research, effective policy, skilled educators, well-managed partnerships and inclusive learning opportunities.

The Platinum tier highlights the organisations and leaders whose work strengthens these foundations.

Recognising institutional excellence encourages better management, evidence-based decision-making, professional standards and partnerships that produce lasting educational benefits.
evidence: Institutional or programme excellence: Effective delivery of the nominated educational service or initiative.
Clear educational objectives: Well-defined needs, beneficiaries and intended results.
Evidence-based implementation: Documented activities, credible research or verifiable policy actions.
Quality and relevance: Services or programmes that respond appropriately to learners, educators or institutions.
Measurable outcomes: Evidence of educational access, quality, participation, skills, research use or other relevant results.
Accountability and sustainability: Responsible governance, resources and continuity.
Wider educational value: Evidence that the contribution strengthens educational practice, institutions or cooperation.

tiers.name: Gold-Blue Garnet Awards
tiers.overview:
The NESA-Africa Gold-Blue Garnet Awards recognise organisations, programmes, initiatives, institutions and eligible public authorities that demonstrate meaningful contributions to education through practical interventions and measurable results.

This tier covers corporate social responsibility, educational technology, media advocacy, NGO programmes, STEM education, creative arts and education policy implementation.

It is designed to recognise educational enablers working in different sectors and at different scales, including those whose contributions may be substantial within a particular community, country, region or educational field.

Gold-Blue Garnet recognition emphasises demonstrated contribution rather than organisational wealth, scale or public visibility.
tiers.why:
Educational development requires participation from businesses, civil society, technology providers, creative professionals, media organisations and public institutions.

These stakeholders help improve school facilities, provide scholarships, develop teaching resources, expand access to technology, support vulnerable learners and promote accountability.

Recognising these contributions encourages responsible collaboration and helps identify practical approaches that can be strengthened or replicated.
evidence: A clearly identified educational need: Evidence that the intervention addresses a relevant problem.
Practical delivery: Verifiable activities, services, products, resources or policies implemented.
Beneficiary impact: Evidence of learners, teachers, schools or communities benefiting.
Appropriate use of resources: Responsible programme management and delivery.
Relevant outcomes: Documented improvements in access, participation, learning, skills, facilities or educational awareness.
Inclusion and accessibility: Appropriate attention to underserved or disadvantaged groups.
Credibility and continuity: Reliable supporting evidence and reasonable prospects for sustained benefit.

awards.title: Best EduTech Innovation for Education (Africa Regional)
awards.overview: Recognises technology products, companies or initiatives that use digital tools to improve teaching, learning, assessment, access or education management in Africa.

evidence: A clearly identified educational problem and suitable technological response.
Evidence of adoption, use and benefit.
Accessibility and relevance to the intended learners or educators.
Appropriate attention to reliability, privacy and sustainability.
Results beyond technical novelty or promotional claims.

subcategories.title: Best EdTech Startup Innovation
subcategories.overview: Recognises an emerging education-technology venture that has developed an innovative solution to a clearly identified educational challenge.
subcategories.why: Startups can introduce new ways to deliver learning, assess progress, connect educators and improve access to educational resources.
subcategories.evidence: A clear educational problem; a working or demonstrably tested solution; evidence of use or pilot results; relevance to intended users; potential for responsible growth.
subcategories.examples: Early-stage EdTech companies and eligible education-technology ventures operating in Africa.

subcategories.title: Best Established EdTech Company Impact
subcategories.overview: Recognises an established education-technology company whose products or services have demonstrated meaningful educational impact.
subcategories.why: Established providers can extend effective learning solutions to larger populations and support institutions over time.
subcategories.evidence: Sustained product or service delivery; evidence of adoption; documented learning or institutional benefits; reliable support; accessibility and responsible data practices.
subcategories.examples: Established EdTech companies serving African learners, educators or educational institutions.

subcategories.title: Best EdTech Social Impact Initiative
subcategories.overview: Recognises a technology-enabled education initiative designed primarily to address a social, access or inclusion challenge.
subcategories.why: Technology can help reach underserved learners when solutions are designed around real barriers and demonstrated needs.
subcategories.evidence: A clearly defined social or educational challenge; evidence of implementation; beneficiaries reached; documented outcomes; attention to affordability, accessibility and sustainability.
subcategories.examples: Non-profit technology initiatives, social enterprises, public-interest digital learning projects and eligible collaborative programmes.

awards.title: Best Media Organisation for Education Advocacy (Nigeria)
awards.overview: Recognises Nigerian media organisations that consistently use journalism, broadcasting or digital communication to improve public understanding of education and support constructive education advocacy.
awards.why: Media can make education challenges visible, inform the public, amplify community voices and encourage accountability.
evidence: Sustained education reporting, programming or advocacy.
Credible, accurate and balanced coverage.
Evidence of audience reach or public engagement.
Documented influence on awareness, participation or educational action.
Responsible treatment of learners and education stakeholders.

subcategories.title: Best Print Media Educational Advocacy
subcategories.overview: Recognises a print media organisation that consistently promotes education through reporting, features, investigations, campaigns or other editorial work.
subcategories.why: Print journalism can explain educational challenges, inform public debate and hold decision-makers accountable.
subcategories.evidence: A body of relevant education coverage; credible reporting; evidence of public engagement; sustained attention to education issues; documented influence or educational value.
subcategories.examples: Newspapers, magazines and other eligible print publications operating in Nigeria.

subcategories.title: Best Radio Educational Programme Excellence
subcategories.overview: Recognises a radio station or programme that uses audio broadcasting to improve educational knowledge, access, participation or awareness.

subcategories.examples: Radio stations and radio programmes providing educational content or advocacy in Nigeria.

subcategories.title: Best Television Educational Content
subcategories.overview: Recognises television content that contributes meaningfully to learning, educational awareness or public understanding of education.

subcategories.evidence: Educational purpose and content quality; suitability for intended audiences; evidence of distribution or reach; accuracy and accessibility; documented learning or awareness benefits.
subcategories.examples: Television broadcasters, educational programme producers and eligible television content initiatives in Nigeria.

subcategories.title: Best Digital & Online Media Educational Advocacy
subcategories.overview: Recognises digital media platforms and online publishers that use digital communication to advance education awareness, access or advocacy.

subcategories.evidence: Sustained education-focused content; credible information; evidence of audience engagement; documented educational action or impact; responsible online communication.
subcategories.examples: Digital publishers, education news platforms, online media organisations and eligible digital advocacy initiatives in Nigeria.

awards.title: Best NGO for Education Advancement (Nigeria)
awards.overview: Recognises Nigerian non-governmental organisations that deliver effective programmes to expand access, improve educational quality or support learners facing barriers to education.
awards.why: NGOs can reach underserved communities, pilot solutions, mobilise volunteers and address needs that are not adequately met by existing services.
evidence: A clear education mission and documented programme delivery.
Evidence of beneficiaries, outcomes and community relevance.
Responsible use of funds and programme resources.
Effective partnerships and safeguarding practices.
Continuity, learning and accountability.

subcategories.title: Best NGO – Basic & Primary Education
subcategories.overview: Recognises an NGO whose work improves access to or quality of basic and primary education in Nigeria.
subcategories.why: Foundational education supports literacy, numeracy, social development and later learning.
subcategories.evidence: Verified programmes serving primary-age learners; evidence of school access or participation; documented improvements in learning conditions or outcomes; responsible programme delivery.
subcategories.examples: NGOs supporting primary schools, foundational learning, early-grade literacy or numeracy in Nigeria.

subcategories.title: Best NGO – Girl-Child Education
subcategories.overview: Recognises an NGO that works to improve girls' access to education, participation, retention, safety or learning outcomes.

subcategories.examples: NGOs supporting girls' scholarships, retention, mentoring, school access or related educational programmes in Nigeria.

subcategories.overview: Recognises an NGO that helps children who are out of school access education, return to learning or participate in suitable alternative learning programmes.

subcategories.examples: NGOs operating school re-entry, catch-up learning, non-formal education or other eligible out-of-school children programmes in Nigeria.

subcategories.overview: Recognises an NGO that improves educational access and participation for learners with disabilities or other additional learning needs.

subcategories.examples: NGOs supporting inclusive schools, disability-inclusive learning, assistive technology or specialist educational services in Nigeria.

subcategories.overview: Recognises an NGO that improves school infrastructure, restores damaged learning facilities or creates safer and more suitable learning environments.

evidence: Verifiable education programming and regional relevance.
Documented reach and outcomes in the communities served.
Effective collaboration with local partners.
Responsible programme delivery and protection of learners.
Evidence of adaptation, sustainability or wider learning.

subcategories.title: Best NGO – Basic & Primary Education
subcategories.overview: Recognises an NGO whose programmes improve foundational and primary education across African communities.

subcategories.evidence: Documented primary education programmes; evidence of learners and communities reached; improvements in access or learning; appropriate local partnerships; credible outcome reporting.
subcategories.examples: NGOs delivering primary or foundational education programmes in African countries or across multiple African communities.

subcategories.overview: Recognises an NGO that advances girls' access to, participation in and completion of education in Africa.

subcategories.overview: Recognises an NGO that expands inclusive educational opportunities for learners with disabilities or additional learning needs in Africa.

subcategories.examples: NGOs supporting inclusive education, disability access, assistive learning and specialist educational support in African communities.

Support for inclusion and access.
Documented improvements in skills, confidence or progression.
